run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:02:26Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real failure evidence localized to the checkout path: frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500 'via_upstream' on POST /api/checkout from 00:02:58Z, frontend recorded error spans on POST /api/checkout and its PlaceOrder client call, and checkout recorded error spans on CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and on its PaymentService/Charge client call. The payment Deployment was restarted at 00:02:43Z with an unchanged pod template (revision 2, only kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt added; identical image and env), its only old pod was deleted at 00:02:46Z, and the replacement payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 00:03:57.877Z (the template defines no readiness probe); checkout logged only '[PlaceOrder]' with no 'payment went through' from 00:03:32 to 00:04:29 and resumed successful pairs at 00:04:42Z. The one fault-injection setting switched on is flagd-config's paymentFailure, state ENABLED, defaultVariant '100%', described 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', which refers to the payment service that was restarted with an unchanged template, and no other object is seen applying a change or fault to payment. It is not verified that this setting was the trigger: every payment charge observed after restart completed successfully ('Transaction complete.'), payment had zero error spans, and the time flagd-config's value was changed cannot be determined (change history not integrated; flagd copies the ConfigMap into an emptyDir only at pod start). The conclusion is therefore partial, with the observed successful charges as counter-evidence to the declared fault.

claims.text: In the 22-minute window ending 2026-11-18T00:23:51Z, frontend-proxy produced error spans on operation 'ingress' (increase 67.05) and operation 'router frontend egress' (increase 60.86) of traces_span_metrics_calls_total, alongside 16841.39 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (span counts, not request counts).

frontend-proxy's own access log shows POST /api/checkout answered with HTTP 500 'via_upstream' from 2026-11-18T00:02:58.071Z through 2026-11-18T00:04:29.071Z (ingress=frontend, e.g. upstream 100.96.5.153:48946, response times 9-1071 ms), while concurrent GET /api/products, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data and POST /api/cart calls in the same log returned 200/308.

frontend recorded error spans on 'POST /api/checkout' (increase 60.86), 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' (60.86) and the client operation 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (60.86) in the 22-minute window, while other frontend operations (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, grpc Cart/AddItem, grpc AdService/GetAds) show 0 error spans.

checkout recorded error spans on the server operation 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (increase 23.22) and on its client operation 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' (increase 23.22) in the 22-minute window.

The payment service recorded zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the 22-minute window (764.37 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans), and its per-minute error series reads 0 at every returned point; no payment operation appears among the returned error-span series.

The error burst is confined to roughly 00:02:58-00:05:26Z: per-minute frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans are 78 (minute ending 00:04:26), 42 (ending 00:05:26), 2 (ending 00:06:26) and 0 (ending 00:03:26), while 5-minute buckets before the burst read 1.25 (ending 23:47:26), 7.78, 1.11, 2.22 and 1.11, and after the burst read 2.15 and 1.18; the burst bucket ending 00:07:26 reads 133.33.

The payment Deployment is at revision 2 and its pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:02:43Z; the template runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with env FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013, and defines no readinessProbe or livenessProbe.

The old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (revision 1, created 2026-11-17T23:29:44Z, replicas 0) and the new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 (revision 2, created 2026-11-18T00:02:43Z, replicas 1) specify the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and an identical env list; the only template difference is the added kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation on the new set.

Events for namespace otel-demo in the window: Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' at 00:02:43Z and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 00:02:46Z; Pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 'Stopping container payment' (Killing, Normal) at 00:02:46Z; Pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled 00:02:43Z, Created 00:02:45Z, Started 00:02:46Z; ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 'Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4' at 00:02:46Z.

The new payment pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 2026-11-18T00:03:57.877Z, about 71 seconds after its container Started event at 00:02:46Z, and only then began logging 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' pairs (first pair 00:04:35.929Z/00:04:36.628Z).

checkout logs between 00:03:32Z and 00:04:29Z contain 33 '[PlaceOrder]' lines and no 'payment went through' or 'order placed' lines, while from 00:04:42Z onward checkout logs alternating 'payment went through' and 'order placed' lines continuously through 00:05:29Z.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) holds fault-injection flag 'paymentFailure' with description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state 'ENABLED' and defaultVariant '100%' (variants off=0, 10%=0.1, 100%=1, 25%=0.25, 50%=0.5, 75%=0.75, 90%=0.95); every other flag in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

flagd runs with command '/flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json' and an init container 'init-config' that copies /config-ro/demo.flagd.json (mounted from ConfigMap flagd-config) into an emptyDir mounted at /etc/flagd; the flagd Deployment's pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:31:32Z, before the incident window.

The payment pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht is Running with its payment container ready, restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated, and all 21 otel-demo pods listed are Running and ready with 0 restarts.

Across all namespaces, the only events involving otel-demo objects in the window are the nine payment rollout events (Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod payment); the remaining events belong to namespace data-recorders (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, Job Completed/SuccessfulCreate, PersistentVolumeClaim provisioning, Pod Created/FailedScheduling/Pulled/Scheduled/Started) and none involve otel-demo services.

The registered Prometheus for this target exposes 63 metric names in the window, including traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket plus container/process/runtime metrics; no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series were returned.

Payment's own container log in the later slice (00:05:23Z-00:12:53Z, newest 60 of 302 matching lines shown) contains only 'Charge request received.' lines with no failure or declined lines, and the 00:05:23.514Z request is immediately followed by 'Transaction complete.'

The declared fault of the switched-on paymentFailure setting was not observed: after the restart every payment charge logged 'Transaction complete.' (00:04:35-00:07:59 slice shows only 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs; 00:05:23-00:12:53 slice shows no failure lines), checkout logged 'payment went through' with 'order placed' from 00:04:42Z onward, and payment's own span error count stayed 0 - so the payment service completed the charges it was observed serving while flagd-config reads '100%'.

Once payment did serve, its gRPC server was listening and the process stayed up: the payment pod is Running/ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, and checkout's Charge calls succeeded from 00:04:42Z, so the failures were confined to the interval before the new container logged its gRPC server start at 00:03:57.877Z.

Rejected: the payment pod was OOMKilled, Evicted or crash-looping. The pod listing shows the current payment container ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated, no OOMKilled/Evicted event exists in the window, and the old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was removed by its own controllers ('Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4' from ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 plus Deployment 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0'), with the replacement given a new name and an unchanged template - a controller-driven rollout, not damage.

Most direct mechanism for the alert: the payment Deployment rollout restart at 00:02:43Z removed the only payment pod at 00:02:46Z, and because the template has no readiness probe the replacement pod was treated as available while its gRPC server did not listen until 00:03:57.877Z, so checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls failed, PlaceOrder failed, frontend /api/checkout returned 500 and frontend-proxy ingress errors rose. Supporting observations are the 500 start at 00:02:58Z, checkout's PlaceOrder-without-payment logs 00:03:32-00:04:29Z, and recovery of payment transactions and checkout successes from ~00:04:35-00:04:42Z.

Second candidate: the switched-on paymentFailure='100%' setting held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the injected fault behind the payment restart and the checkout errors. This remains unconfirmed - payment charge requests were observed to complete successfully, so the flag's declared 100% charge-failure behavior was not seen, and flagd copies the ConfigMap into an emptyDir only at pod start (flagd last restarted 23:31:32Z), so whether the current 100% value was being served at 00:02-00:05Z is unknown.

Other error spans in the window are background, not part of this incident: ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each show about 1.03 error spans on flagd EventStream evaluation operations, and frontend-proxy already showed 1.11-7.78 error spans per 5-minute bucket before the burst (e.g. 1.25 at 23:47:26), far below the 133.33 burst bucket.

Verify what the flagd instance is actually serving (flagd-ui / OFREP port 8016) and when flagd-config's paymentFailure was changed; if the 100% value is intended, restart flagd so the init-config copy picks it up, and if not, set it back to 'off'. Confirm this before treating the setting as causal.

Add a readiness probe to the payment container (and to other otel-demo workloads that lack one) so a rolling restart cannot route Charge traffic to a pod whose gRPC server is not yet listening, which is the mechanism that produced the 500s here.

Establish who or what set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:02:43Z on Deployment payment (kubectl rollout restart or an automated action) using change/audit history, which is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: The trigger of the payment Deployment restart at 2026-11-18T00:02:43Z is unknown: the change_history integration is not available, and the evidence only shows the resulting rollout (restartedAt annotation, ReplicaSet replacement, pod delete/create).

It cannot be determined when flagd-config's paymentFailure was changed to '100%' (no change history; the ConfigMap object was created 2026-11-17T23:29:43Z and flagd copies it into an emptyDir only at pod start), nor whether flagd was serving that value during 00:02-00:05Z.

flagd's container logs were not obtainable: the log query for pod flagd-869c45cb9d-rsjs7 returned status no_data with 0 bytes read for the init-config, flagd and flagd-ui streams (evidence 6a28b1a5-c388-4a9c-b412-7b2abf279184, not citable), so flag reload/evaluation activity is unknown, not absent.

Jaeger trace searches for frontend-proxy and checkout in 00:02-00:08Z and 00:18-00:23:51Z returned status no_data (backend_traces_returned 0), and the unrestricted searches were RESULT_TOO_LARGE; the newest Jaeger data returned in this Run is 2026-11-17T23:50:51Z, so the error status detail/message of the failing Charge and PlaceOrder spans during the burst is unknown.

The frontend container log stream for frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc returned 0 bytes / 0 lines (status no_data, filter not run), so the frontend application's own error text for the 500 responses could not be read.

The checkout container log filter for error/charge keywords returned no matching lines (status no_data, 6945 lines removed by filter); only unfiltered checkout log slices were usable, so any Charge failure text inside checkout is unconfirmed.

No rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exist in this Prometheus (queries returned status no_data), so gRPC status-code and server-request error-rate breakdowns for payment/checkout/frontend-proxy could not be checked.
The alert annotation's error-rate definition (0.011111) could not be reproduced; traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans, not requests, so the alert's exact metric expression is unverified.

Kubernetes object state was read after the window; the old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 no longer exists, so its container logs and exact termination details could not be inspected (fetch_pod_logs reported no previous container instance for payment, checkout and frontend).

Four log views were delivered with incomplete=true because their limits cut lines (payment limit 60 of 302 and 200 of 277, checkout limit 60 of 1271, frontend-proxy limit 80 of 104), so unshown lines of those streams are unknown rather than absent.
next_steps: Check the cluster audit log or GitOps/Helm history for the actor that set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:02:43Z on Deployment otel-demo/payment.
Query flagd's OFREP endpoint / flagd-ui for the effective value of paymentFailure and compare it with the flagd-config ConfigMap value to see whether the running flagd serves the current file.
Review edit history for ConfigMap flagd-config (and the Helm values that generated it, chart opentelemetry-demo-0.38.6, release otel-demo) to date the paymentFailure='100%' change.
Add monitoring of payment pod availability/readiness around rollouts (no readinessProbe is defined) so a rolling restart cannot silently drop the only payment instance.
